We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2})(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-2\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,dx \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-2\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-2(-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}+D) \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-2D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={[{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & ={(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})+\frac{2(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})}{3}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})}{9} \\  & \,-((0)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+\frac{2(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)}{3}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)}{9}) \\  & =-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}+0+\frac{2}{9}-0 \\  & =\frac{8-9{\pi }^{2}}{36} \\  & =\frac{8-9{\pi }^{2}}{36}\end{aligned}
$$
